notes:
Both set-synonymity and set-contiguity use inherently symmetric relationships (synonym pairs, mutual-touching pairs) where no word order can be inferred, per the integrity and test-player findings. Fixing this requires swapping in pairs with a genuinely directional relationship, not just reordering existing words.
- set-synonymity: stove:range and skillet:frying pan are pure synonym pairs with no inherent direction, so the leading word in each pair is arbitrary and unguessable, and a solver can't infer which side comes first — flagged as order-indistinguishable and order-guessed.
  Try: Replace the relationship with a directional one (e.g., 'generic term : specific brand-name term' or 'informal : formal name') and author new pairs that fit, such as fridge:refrigerator and freezer:deep freezer, where direction is inferable from register.
  Or: If synonymity must stay, author pairs with a clear register gap in one consistent direction (e.g., colloquial term first, technical term second) rather than near-perfect synonyms like stove/range.
  Or: Drop set-synonymity and author a replacement set entirely with a non-symmetric relationship (e.g., container:contents) using new kitchen words.
- set-contiguity: backsplash:countertop and baseboard:cabinet are defined by mutual touching, which is symmetric by definition — order-indistinguishable, matching the coast:ocean failure mode exactly.
  Try: Replace with a directional spatial relationship (e.g., 'fixture : the surface it protects' framed as protector→protected) and author new pairs that clearly point one way, such as backsplash:wall and toe-kick:cabinet base, where one item exists specifically to shield the other.
  Or: Author pairs using a whole-part or covers/covered-by relation instead of contiguity, e.g., countertop:cabinet (rests-on) and backsplash:wall (mounted-on), each with one inferable direction.
  Or: Drop set-contiguity and author a replacement set with an inherently asymmetric kitchen-fixture relationship (e.g., 'fixture : material it's made from').
Do not change: set-tool-action, set-dimensional — no allowlisted finding touches them.

persisted.note: Read as informal-pair vs formal-pair for the same two appliance categories, both halves carry the identical register-shift relation. Both halves read as: "two sibling appliances named informally" and "the same two sibling appliances named formally".

Because fridge/refrigerator and freezer/deep freezer are pure synonym pairs, swapping which register is used for which appliance still yields the same underlying sibling-appliance relation on both sides. Both halves read as: "informal name of one appliance next to formal name of its sibling" and "formal name of one appliance next to informal name of its sibling".

All four items sit on one size continuum, and both halves consistently pair items from the small end and the large end, so the smaller:smaller :: larger:larger reading holds. Both halves read as: "two smaller cookware items (co-size, cross-kind)" and "two larger cookware items (co-size, cross-kind)".

Flipping the right pair to ramekin:stockpot gives smaller:larger on both sides, matching saucepan:roasting pan, since all four sit on the same size dimension. Both halves read as: "smaller vessel to larger vessel (cross-kind)" and "larger vessel to smaller vessel (cross-kind) as given, but flips to smaller:larger".
